answer: One fix I like is making graders also guess how the rest of the panel will vote. Pay goes to votes that turn out more common than people predicted, which is how the truth serum idea from survey research works. A clone farm knows exactly how its bloc will vote, so its guesses match its own ballots and its votes are never a surprise. That kills its grading pay. Say a job checks juniper die-off data from a tundra survey. To swing it the farm has to vote as one and eat that loss on every panel, and spreading out to look honest means it isn't swinging anything. Easy wins become a comet sighting.
